items.title: Feature request: lossless, portable Codex project/session export-import for cross-device and Git workflows

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: session
labels.description: Issues involving session (thread) management, resuming, forking, naming, archiving

items.body:
### What feature would you like to see?

Please add an **official, supported Codex Project + Session export/import format** that allows a project to be moved to another computer and reopened **without losing its Codex working context**.

The goal is not merely to sync source code or produce a summary such as `AGENTS.md`. I want a durable, portable representation of the **actual Codex project and its sessions**.

### 1. Lossless session/project restoration

After exporting a Codex project on machine A and importing/opening it on machine B, Codex should immediately be able to access the same durable session context, including as applicable:

- Full user/assistant conversation history
- Tool-call history and results
- Terminal command history and captured command output
- Debugging results, logs, stack traces, test output, experiment results, and other generated evidence
- Diffs/patches and Codex-produced changes
- Session metadata, titles, timestamps, task state, and relationships between sessions
- Project metadata and repository/worktree association
- Attachments or generated artifacts referenced by the session, where they are part of the durable Codex record

This should be a **supported round-trip format**, not a best-effort summary and not a dependency on undocumented internal SQLite/JSONL layouts.

The important acceptance criterion is:

> Export on machine A -> copy/clone to machine B -> import/open -> Codex can continue with the same historical context without requiring the user to manually reconstruct prior discussions, debugging evidence, or experiment results.

I am referring to durable session/project state, not a byte-for-byte VM/RAM snapshot of a currently running debugger process.

### 2. Self-contained, portable project directory

Please support storing/exporting the Codex project state in **one directory associated with the repository**, for example:

```text
MyProject/
├── .git/
├── src/
├── AGENTS.md
└── .codex-project/
    ├── manifest.json
    ├── sessions/
    ├── artifacts/
    ├── debug-results/
    └── index/
```

The exact layout is not important, but it should have these properties:

- Self-contained and easy to archive, copy, back up, and move
- Uses a versioned, documented schema
- Uses relative/project-root-aware paths so a project can move from `C:\...` to `D:\...` or to another OS where possible
- Supports integrity/version checking during import
- Does not require copying the user's entire global `CODEX_HOME`
- Clearly separates portable project state from machine-specific state, credentials, secrets, caches, and transient processes

A simple workflow could be something like:

```text
codex project export --output .codex-project/
codex project import .codex-project/
```

or, ideally, Codex Desktop could recognize the project metadata automatically when the repository is opened.

### 3. Git-friendly and collaboration-friendly

The portable Codex project directory should be designed to work well with Git so that a team can optionally version and share Codex context together with the source repository.

Important properties:

- Stable, documented, preferably text/JSON/JSONL-based formats where practical
- Deterministic or low-noise files so Git diffs remain useful
- Large/binary artifacts can be separated or optionally handled via Git LFS
- Clear `.gitignore` guidance for caches, temporary files, credentials, and machine-specific state
- No secrets or local credentials included by default
- Multiple developers should be able to clone a repository and recover the shared Codex project/session history
- Provenance should be preserved so it is clear which session/user/machine produced a result
- Ideally support merging or at least safely coexisting session histories from multiple contributors without corrupting project state

This would make Codex projects behave more like a portable development workspace/solution rather than a collection of machine-local UI state.

### Why this matters

For long-running engineering work, `AGENTS.md`, summaries, or manually maintained context files are useful but inherently lossy. They often preserve the current conclusion while losing:

- why earlier approaches were rejected,
- exact error messages and stack traces,
- commands and outputs,
- failed experiments,
- intermediate debugging evidence,
- and the chronology that led to an architectural decision.

That information can be critical months later.

A supported lossless project/session format would also solve several operational problems:

- moving between workstation and laptop,
- rebuilding or replacing a development machine,
- backing up Codex work,
- disaster recovery,
- team handoff,
- auditability/reproducibility,
- and keeping AI-assisted engineering context next to the source code.

### Related existing requests

This request overlaps with, but is intentionally broader than:

- #13267 — export the entire session
- #21803 — cross-device sync for Codex Projects and Chats
- #32350 — cloud sync for Codex Projects across devices
- #38838 — session storage, backups, and export

Those requests address important parts of the problem. The additional requirement here is a **documented, lossless, round-trippable, project-scoped format that can live in one directory and optionally be versioned with Git for cross-device use and team collaboration**.

Thanks for considering this.

items.title: Feature request: external wake / message injection for an existing Codex Desktop or CLI session

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: app-server
labels.description: Issues involving app server protocol or interfaces

items.body:
### What feature would you like to see?

Please add a supported way for an external local process to wake an **existing, currently open Codex Desktop or interactive CLI session** and start a new turn in that same conversation.

The core use case is a long-running background watcher (for example, a market/daywatch process, CI monitor, build watcher, alerting service, or local automation) that should be able to do:

```
external event
  -> existing Codex session/thread
  -> start a new turn automatically
  -> response appears in the already-open Codex UI/CLI conversation
```

without minute-level polling and without starting a separate session/process that the user has to inspect elsewhere.

### Current limitation

Tested on Windows with:

- Codex Desktop: `0.155.0-alpha.9.2`
- Codex CLI: `0.155.1`

The App Server already exposes useful primitives such as `thread/read`, `thread/resume`, and `turn/start`, but an external App Server process cannot take control of a thread that is owned by the running Desktop app.

In a clean idle test:

- the active turn emitted `task_complete`
- an external helper waited ~150 ms
- `thread/read` showed all turns completed and no `inProgress` turns
- the external `thread/resume` request was sent ~365 ms after `task_complete`
- the thread writer lock still existed
- `thread/resume` failed with:

```
thread <id> already has an active writer
```

So the Desktop appears to retain writer ownership even while the thread is idle.

At the same time, the Desktop's App Server instance does not expose a supported external listener/control channel that another local process can attach to. That means an external watcher cannot route a new `turn/start` through the same App Server that already owns the UI thread.

### Requested capability

Any one of the following would solve the problem:

1. **Attach to the running Desktop/CLI App Server**
   - supported local socket / named pipe / control transport
   - authenticated local connection
   - allows external clients to submit input to an existing thread owned by that App Server

2. **Session inbox / external message API**
   - send a message to an existing session/thread
   - if the session is idle, automatically start a new turn
   - surface the new turn and assistant output in the already-open UI/CLI conversation

3. **External wake / trigger API**
   - event-driven trigger for an existing thread
   - no polling requirement
   - preserves the current conversation context

### Suggested acceptance criteria

- A Codex Desktop or interactive CLI session is open and idle.
- A separate local process can send a message/event to that exact existing session.
- Codex automatically starts a new turn.
- The new user/event input and assistant response appear in the same currently-open conversation.
- No second interactive session is created.
- No minute-level polling is required.
- The mechanism is documented and supported, including Windows.

### Why this matters

Codex already has most of the building blocks for long-running agent workflows, but the missing bridge is **external event -> existing UI session**.

This would unlock practical always-on automations such as:

- CI/build alerts
- market/data watchers
- log/incident monitors
- file or repository watchers
- scheduled/background processes
- local agent orchestration

while keeping all context and output in the conversation the user is already working in.

Thanks — this would make Codex much more usable as a persistent, event-driven local agent rather than only a request/response tool.

items.title: Record terminal outcome and OpenTelemetry status on turn spans

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

labels.name: agent
labels.description: Issues related to the core agent loop

items.body:
### What variant of Codex are you using?

CLI/app-server with `otel.trace_exporter` enabled.

### What feature would you like to see?

Please record the terminal outcome on the core-owned turn span (`session_task.turn` and the other `SessionTask::span_name()` values). Today these spans close with OpenTelemetry status `UNSET` regardless of whether the turn completed or failed, so trace consumers cannot calculate turn reliability without incorrectly inferring it from child API or tool spans.

Suggested contract:

- successful terminal completion: `codex.turn.outcome = "completed"` and `otel.status_code = "OK"`
- terminal Codex error or unexpected `SessionTask` error: `codex.turn.outcome = "failed"` and `otel.status_code = "ERROR"`
- intentional cancellation/replacement: `codex.turn.outcome = "aborted"`, plus low-cardinality `codex.turn.abort_reason`; leave OTel status `UNSET` because cancellation is not necessarily a failed operation

Child tool failures should remain independent: a failed tool call that Codex recovers from should not mark the turn failed.

### Additional information

The turn span is created in `codex-rs/core/src/tasks/mod.rs::start_task`. Normal terminal outcomes are known in `Session::on_task_finished`; externally aborted tasks are handled in `handle_task_abort`, so retaining a clone of the span in `RunningTask` covers that path before the task handle is aborted. `ErrorEvent::affects_turn_status()` already provides the right filter for terminal errors.

I prototyped and validated this mapping locally with an `InMemorySpanExporter`: completed exports `Status::Ok`, failed exports `Status::Error`, and aborted remains `Status::Unset` while carrying `codex.turn.outcome=aborted` and the abort reason. The focused test passes, and `cargo clippy --tests -p codex-core` is clean for the changed code.

This also avoids putting error messages into span attributes/status descriptions.

Add streaming coverage comparing character-by-character output with complete rendering at wide and narrow widths in rich and raw modes.

items.body:
### What variant of Codex are you using?

CLI (`codex-cli 0.155.1`, macOS 26.5.2 arm64)

### What feature would you like to see?

Please register **Osaurus** as a built-in OSS provider alongside `ollama` and `lmstudio`, so that

```
codex --oss --local-provider osaurus
```

and

```toml
oss_provider = "osaurus"
```

work the same way the existing two local providers do.

[Osaurus](https://github.com/dinoki-ai/osaurus) is a native macOS (Apple Silicon / MLX) local model server. It already speaks the Responses API that Codex requires, on the same contract the two existing OSS arms rely on:

- `POST http://127.0.0.1:1337/v1/responses` (streaming SSE, `function_call` / `function_call_output` items, `strict: false` tools, `store: false`, `include: ["reasoning.encrypted_content"]` all accepted)
- `GET http://127.0.0.1:1337/v1/models` for model discovery
- no auth needed on loopback (a Bearer key is required only when the user enables network exposure, exactly like a custom provider with `env_key`)
- models are already downloaded and managed by the app, so there is no pull/download step for Codex to drive — readiness is a reachability probe.

#### Working today as a custom provider

This config works end to end with Codex 0.155.1 (proof below); the request is only to make the same thing available without hand-editing `config.toml`:

```toml
# ~/.codex/config.toml
[model_providers.osaurus]
name = "Osaurus"
base_url = "http://127.0.0.1:1337/v1"
wire_api = "responses"

# ~/.codex/osaurus.config.toml  (codex --profile osaurus)
model = "raptor-0.6-4b-jang_6m"
model_provider = "osaurus"
model_context_window = 1048576
```

Osaurus is adding a Settings → Server card that generates and writes exactly this config for users, so a built-in provider would mostly remove the `--profile` step and enable the `--oss` picker / auto-select flow.

#### Exact touch points (current `main`, `d1092865f8ec63735006211f65ee109ce91c30b9`)

I know external PRs are not accepted, so here is the scoped change for whoever picks it up:

- `codex-rs/model-provider-info/src/lib.rs`: add `OSAURUS_OSS_PROVIDER_ID = "osaurus"` and `DEFAULT_OSAURUS_PORT: u16 = 1337`, and register it in `built_in_model_providers` via `create_oss_provider(DEFAULT_OSAURUS_PORT, WireApi::Responses)` next to the `ollama` / `lmstudio` entries.
- `codex-rs/utils/oss/src/lib.rs`: arms in `get_default_model_for_oss_provider` and `ensure_oss_provider_ready`. Osaurus needs only a reachability check against `/v1/models` (there is no download step); the default model can be the first entry `/v1/models` returns, since the installed set is user-managed.
- `codex-rs/tui/src/oss_selection.rs`: a third `SelectOption` in `OSS_SELECT_OPTIONS`, and include Osaurus in the "only one local server is running → auto-select" logic.
- `codex-rs/config/src/config_toml.rs`: extend `validate_oss_provider` (and its error string) and the `oss_provider` doc comment; mirror the description in `codex-rs/core/config.schema.json`.

I understand the comment in `built_in_model_providers` about not wanting to adjudicate third-party providers. If the bar is "widely used local runtime with a conformant Responses endpoint", Osaurus is asking to be measured against the same bar as LM Studio; if the answer is that the custom-provider path is the intended route, that is fine too and this issue can be closed — the custom-provider config above already works.

### Additional information

Live proof, Codex 0.155.1 (`npx @openai/codex@0.155.1`) against an Osaurus development build on macOS 26.5.2 (Apple M4 Pro, 48 GB), model `raptor-0.6-4b-jang_6m` (OsaurusAI Raptor 0.6 4B, JANG 6-bit), `codex exec --profile osaurus --json`:

Turn 1 (tool call → result → answer, `turn.completed`):

```
{"type":"item.started","item":{"id":"item_1","type":"command_execution","command":"/bin/zsh -lc 'cat notes.txt'", ...}}
{"type":"item.completed","item":{"id":"item_1","type":"command_execution","command":"/bin/zsh -lc 'cat notes.txt'","aggregated_output":"The secret word is PTERODACTYL.\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}
{"type":"item.completed","item":{"id":"item_2","type":"agent_message","text":"PTERODACTYL"}}
{"type":"turn.completed","usage":{"input_tokens":16084,"cached_input_tokens":0,"cache_write_input_tokens":0,"output_tokens":17,"reasoning_output_tokens":0}}
```

Turn 2 (`codex exec resume --last`, history replayed with `function_call`, `function_call_output`, and the assistant `output_text` message; second tool call grounded on that history):

```
{"type":"item.completed","item":{"id":"item_1","type":"command_execution","command":"/bin/zsh -lc \"printf '%s' 'PTERODACTYL' | wc -c\"","aggregated_output":"      11\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}
{"type":"item.completed","item":{"id":"item_2","type":"agent_message","text":"11"}}
{"type":"turn.completed","usage":{"input_tokens":32388,"cached_input_tokens":0,"cache_write_input_tokens":0,"output_tokens":43,"reasoning_output_tokens":0}}
```

Server-side generation for the turn-1 answer measured 50.7 tok/s on this model (8081 prompt tokens as counted by Osaurus; the 16084 above is Codex's fallback-metadata estimate, which also explains the harmless `Model metadata for 'raptor-0.6-4b-jang_6m' not found` notice at thread start).

One observation that may be useful for other OSS providers: Codex sends `reasoning: {"summary": "auto"}` with no `effort`, echoes prior `function_call` items without `status`, and replays assistant messages with `output_text` content parts. All three are valid Responses input, and Osaurus had to loosen its decoder for each of them to get past the first tool call — worth keeping in mind when validating a new OSS arm.

items.body:
### What variant of Codex are you using?

CLI — the interactive Rust TUI (`codex`), not the Codex desktop app.

### What feature would you like to see?

Codex CLI should have a protected way for the agent to request a third-party credential without asking the user to paste it into chat or exposing its plaintext to the model.

A typical flow would be:

1. The model requests a credential by name, for example `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`.
2. The TUI opens a masked local input prompt.
3. The user chooses whether to keep it for this session or remember it for this project.
4. The model receives only the credential name and availability status.
5. Codex injects the value locally into approved command environments, for example as `CODEX_SECRET_OPENROUTER_API_KEY`.
6. Codex replaces the exact value with `Hide(OPENROUTER_API_KEY)` before command output, logs, rollout history, hooks, or tool results can expose it to the model.

The private answer must bypass normal chat input and must never become a conversation item. Project credentials should be encrypted at rest, with the encryption key held by macOS Keychain, a Linux native persistent keyring, or Windows Credential Manager. If secure storage is unavailable, persistent storage should fail closed while session-only use remains available.

Suggested acceptance criteria:

- Masked credential entry is implemented in the CLI/TUI.
- Canceling the prompt registers no credential.
- The plaintext is absent from model requests, rollout history, TUI history, logs, and hook/tool metadata.
- Local commands can receive the credential without putting it in command text.
- Streaming stdout/stderr and final command results are redacted before model-visible persistence.
- Session-only credentials disappear when the thread closes.
- Project credentials can be restored after Codex restarts.
- The behavior works on macOS, Linux, and Windows.

### Additional information

I built a tested reference implementation for the Rust CLI/TUI:

- Draft fork PR: https://github.com/dajun666/codex/pull/1
- Implementation branch: https://github.com/dajun666/codex/tree/feat/private-project-secrets
- Real TUI recording and test evidence: https://github.com/dajun666/codex-private-project-credentials-demo

The recording shows the actual forked TUI performing masked input, lifetime selection, local environment injection, and model-visible output redaction.

Focused validation on current `main`:

- `codex-core` request-secret integration tests: 3 passed, including restoration by a second Codex instance.
- `codex-secrets`: 14 passed.
- TUI masked-input snapshot: passed.
- app-server private-input transport: passed.
- Gitleaks and GitHub secret scanning: no findings.

Related issues cover different parts of the problem: #25585 requests pre-submit secret detection, #31545 proposes secret-file/output hardening, #34233 reports secret leakage through CLI tool output, and #36854 concerns credentials specifically for plugin-provided MCP servers. This request is for a general protected credential-ingress and runtime-injection mechanism in the interactive CLI/TUI.

items.title: Preserve empty cell metadata under pending tool-call pressure
items.body:
Preserve empty cell metadata under pending tool-call pressure

## Why

Reaching the pending tool-call limit could evict finished empty cells even though removing them frees no pending-call capacity. This loses the metadata needed to certify an empty tool-call inventory on a later `wait`.

## What changed

Only evict cells with pending calls when reclaiming pending-call capacity. Keep empty cells eligible for eviction when a cell slot is needed.

## Testing

Extend recorder coverage to check empty inventories under pending-call pressure in fresh and resumed sessions. Add a code-mode integration test verifying that `wait` serializes an empty inventory with `tool_calls_complete: true` while another cell has filled the pending-call budget.

Even completely benign follow-up messages, including a single character such as `1`, are blocked again with the same `cyber_policy` error.

`01a0c19e-97a7-7832-8e72-c251e5901f18`

This makes the behavior unpredictable and difficult to recover from.

For developers working on RTC, networking, multimedia, or systems programming, terms such as UDP, P2P, socket, EINTR, Windows APIs, Linux APIs, codecs, and low-latency transport are normal engineering topics. A benign RTC/C++ systems programming discussion should not trigger `cyber_policy`.

Add explicit gateway login control and authentication status

## What changed

- Add `GatewayLoginControl` so hosts can require caller-initiated browser authorization while retaining automatic login by default.
- Expose passive readiness checks, scoped status subscriptions, and cancellable browser login that reports success after credentials are persisted.
- Return non-retryable request errors for `LoginRequired` and `LoginInProgress`, while preserving retries for transient authentication failures.
- Keep rejected credentials unready until replaced, and prevent slow readiness reads from blocking cached requests or overwriting newer credentials.

## Testing

Add coverage for login cancellation, status notifications, external credential recovery, concurrent credential I/O, legacy automatic login, and request retry behavior.
